assigned.title: The sidecar half of the desktop contract was never wired into the server
assigned.acceptance:
PW-0101 designed the sidecar contract and PW-0102 built the shell that speaks it. NOTHING CONNECTED THE SIDECAR HALF. Three symptoms, all found in round 95 by starting the packaged artefact for the first time -- none is reachable by any existing test, because until the packaging corrective landed there was no packaged sidecar to start.

1. THE HANDSHAKE IS NEVER EMITTED. `lib/sidecar/handshake.ts` exports `formatHandshake` and `HANDSHAKE_PREFIX`; the only caller in the repository is its own test. The packaged server's complete stdout is Next's banner plus the catalog line -- no `liberty-sidecar-ready`. `shell.rs` waits for that line, times out, kills the child and reports `NoHandshake`. THE INSTALLED APPLICATION THEREFORE NEVER OPENS A WINDOW ON CONTENT.

2. THE EXPECTED HOST CANNOT MATCH. `sidecar.rs` sets LIBERTY_SIDECAR_HOST to BIND_HOST, the bare literal "127.0.0.1". `policy.ts`'s `authorizeRequest` compares it to the request's `Host` header with `!==`, and its comment requires exactness: "127.0.0.1:3000 and 127.0.0.1:3001 are different listeners". A Host header always carries a non-default port, so the comparison can never succeed. `policy.test.ts` uses "127.0.0.1:3100" -- an authority -- so the policy side expects host:port and the shell side sends a hostname. Each half is self-consistent; the pair is not.
   PROVEN BY A ONE-VARIABLE COMPARISON against the packaged tree: with "127.0.0.1" every route answered 403; with "127.0.0.1:<bound port>" /, /search, /profiles, /api/health and /title/<id> answered 200, the stylesheet 200 and a client chunk 200.

3. THE BIND-SAFETY GATE IS NOT WIRED IN. `checkBindSafety` refuses to start a sidecar that would bind 0.0.0.0 -- 'a sidecar inheriting a container's HOSTNAME would serve the whole network with a valid token that the user's own browser holds'. `proxy.ts` calls `readSidecarEnvironment` but NOTHING calls `checkBindSafety`. A written, tested security control that no code path reaches.

THE ORDERING PROBLEM THAT MAKES 2 NON-TRIVIAL, and the reason this needs a ruling rather than a patch: the expected host must contain the port, and BIND_PORT is "0" so the port does not exist until after the child binds. `handshake.ts` records why that was chosen -- the shell picking a port has a TOCTOU window and 'the user sees a blank window'. So either the sidecar derives its own authority after binding (a change in `lib/sidecar/**`), or the shell reserves a port (which reverses a reviewed decision), or the comparison changes shape (which its own comment argues against). ALL THREE ARE ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS; pick one deliberately.

REQUIRED: the packaged sidecar emits exactly one handshake line on stdout, and the shell reaches a window.
REQUIRED: a request from the shell's own WebView is AUTHORIZED, with the port question settled one way and the reasoning recorded.
REQUIRED: `checkBindSafety` is consulted before the listener accepts anything, and a sidecar that would bind non-loopback refuses to start.
REQUIRED: A TEST THAT COMPOSES THE TWO HALVES. Every one of these defects is a pair of self-consistent unit tests with nothing between them. Whatever form it takes -- a harness that starts the packaged server with the environment `plan_launch` produces and asserts an authorized request succeeds -- the property is that the shell's output and the sidecar's input are checked against each other rather than each against its own fixture.

NOT IN SCOPE: packaging (PW-0501), the Job Object, the launch token's minting, and anything requiring attended Windows hardware (PW-0103).
assigned.notes:
PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 95, created unowned rather than claimed, on the PW-0501 precedent. Found during PW-0501's qualification by starting the packaged sidecar -- the first time this project has run one. P0 because it is the difference between an installer that produces a working application and one that produces a window that never loads, and because PW-0603's certification sheet and PW-0103's experiment both sit downstream of a shell that can actually reach its own server.
SURFACE NOTE: spans apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/** and apps/desktop/src-tauri/, which is unusual and is the point -- the defect IS the seam between them, and a task confined to one side would reproduce the two-self-consistent-halves problem that caused it. PW-0501 currently holds apps/desktop/**, so these two must not be active at the same time; the overlap is real and is resolved by sequence, the same way PW-0102 and PW-0501 were.
WHAT PW-0501 STILL PROVES WITHOUT THIS: that CI produces an installer, that it installs and uninstalls, and that the packaged tree serves pages when given a correct environment. It has never claimed the application launches, and `.github/workflows/windows.yml` says so in its header.

typecheck.evidence:
`npm run typecheck` -> "Tasks: 22 successful, 22 total" (turbo, all packages). `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json` exits 0 with no diagnostics after the final wording correction to `host_not_stated`. `npm run lint` -> "Tasks: 12 successful, 12 total", 0 errors; the single warning (`WatchlistEntryRow` unused in `in-memory-repository.test.ts`) predates this task and is outside its surface. `npm run repo:validate` -> "Project Liberty repository validation passed." `npm run ai:validate` -> valid, 106 tasks, 9 agents.

WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT IS THE POINT OF THE CHANGE: making `listeningPort` a REQUIRED third parameter of `authorizeRequest`, rather than one defaulted to null, turned "which call sites still judge a request without the port" into a compiler error. It found exactly one production call site (`apps/web/src/proxy.ts`) and ten test call sites. A defaulted parameter would have compiled, shipped, and silently judged every production request under the reduced contract.

unit.evidence:
`npm run test` -> 74 test files, 1308 tests, all passing (@liberty/web), 22/22 turbo tasks successful. The sidecar surface specifically: `npx vitest run apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/` -> 4 files, 63 tests passing -- policy.test.ts 33 (was 18), bootstrap.test.ts 14 (new), listener.test.ts 11 (new), handshake.test.ts 5 (unchanged).

THE REGRESSION PROPERTIES REQUIREMENT D ASKS FOR, EACH WITH THE FILE THAT HOLDS IT:
 1. the bind check runs on the real startup path and refuses a short token -- bootstrap.test.ts
 2. a refusal exits non-zero -- bootstrap.test.ts (every refusal case asserts exit [1])
 3. a refusal emits NO handshake -- bootstrap.test.ts
 4. the diagnostic names the variable and the minimum, and never the token value -- bootstrap.test.ts
 5. a hosted deployment is untouched: no check, no diagnostic, no exit, no handshake, no published port -- bootstrap.test.ts
 6. the handshake carries the ACTUAL bound port, never the requested PORT -- bootstrap.test.ts (PORT=0 in the environment, listener on 52341, asserts 52341 and asserts the line does not contain "port":0)
 7. exactly one handshake per process even when the startup path runs twice -- bootstrap.test.ts
 8. the handshake is the only line on stdout and carries the prefix the shell scans for -- bootstrap.test.ts
 9. the emitted line round-trips through `parseHandshake`, the parser the Rust side's contract is written against -- bootstrap.test.ts
10. the port is published for the request path BEFORE the line is printed -- bootstrap.test.ts
11. an ACTUAL non-loopback bind is refused even when the environment claimed loopback -- bootstrap.test.ts
12. an unestablishable or ambiguous bound port is a refusal, not a guess -- bootstrap.test.ts + listener.test.ts
13. sockets are not mistaken for listeners -- listener.test.ts (an outbound socket's ephemeral local port is the intermittent, production-only, under-load-only failure this prevents)
14. Host validation is hostname-exact: suffix, prefix, userinfo, 0.0.0.0, LAN, alternate loopback spellings and DNS names are all refused -- policy.test.ts
15. a malformed authority is refused rather than repaired: URL delimiters, whitespace, control characters, multi-colon unbracketed, non-decimal / out-of-range / zero-padded port, trailing dot, zone-scoped literal -- policy.test.ts
16. a Host naming the right hostname but a different port is refused when the port is known -- policy.test.ts
17. when the port is UNKNOWN the hostname and token are still enforced and the guard does not fall open -- policy.test.ts
18. a failing bind check refuses every request at the request boundary, closing the window between `listen()` and `exit(1)` -- policy.test.ts
19. one refusal shape for every failure, so the wire is not an oracle -- policy.test.ts (6 distinct failures, one JSON shape)
20. the port memo caches a hit and never a miss, so asking too early cannot freeze the answer to "unknown" -- listener.test.ts

Twenty, not sixteen; the extra four are 10, 13, 19 and 20, each of which is a failure mode found while implementing rather than one gpt-architect named.

assigned.title: PORT=0 never reaches the kernel: the packaged sidecar always tries to bind 3000
assigned.acceptance:
The packaged desktop sidecar binds a port the KERNEL chose, on 127.0.0.1, and reports it. Set by
gpt-architect's round-96 ruling; the twelve evidence items below are theirs, quoted in substance.

REQUIRED DIRECTION (theirs): keep the Next standalone output as the request handler; introduce the
smallest supported desktop-specific bootstrap that creates the HTTP listener explicitly on host
127.0.0.1 and port 0; read the actual port from server.address() after the listen callback; emit the
existing single handshake line with that port; preserve every PW-0105 control (per-launch token,
request authorization, Host validation, bind-safety, fail-closed, no LAN bind, no source-checkout
dependency); do not patch generated Next output after every build unless there is no stable supported
composition point; and if the public APIs cannot do it without unstable internals, STOP and document
the exact limitation before choosing another design.

FORBIDDEN, restated so a later round cannot reintroduce it: the shell must not probe for or preselect
a free TCP port. No portpicker. No bind-then-retry-higher loop.

ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE, all twelve:
 1. launch with port 3000 deliberately occupied
 2. the packaged sidecar still starts successfully
 3. the actual listener port is not 3000 in that test
 4. the handshake contains the real bound port
 5. the shell parser accepts it
 6. all required routes serve successfully
 7. static / CSS / client assets load
 8. token and Host attack cases still fail
 9. non-loopback startup fails
10. nothing writes beside the executable
11. repeated launches can use different kernel-selected ports
12. no shell-side free-port probing exists
PLUS regression coverage "specifically preventing PORT=0 from silently becoming 3000 again".

AND A NINE-ITEM REPORT: bootstrap architecture chosen; whether only public/stable Next APIs are used;
exact proof with 3000 occupied; real bound port observed; handshake evidence; route/static/security test
results; Windows/Linux differences; commits; gate state; delivery bundle/apply script.
assigned.notes:
RULED BY gpt-architect IN ROUND 96 -- proceed, with the required direction in `acceptance`. The original
proposal notes are superseded by that ruling; what follows is what round 96 established empirically and
why the task has not started.

THE DEFECT, UNCHANGED. Next 16.3.1's generated standalone entry reads
`const currentPort = parseInt(process.env.PORT, 10) || 3000` and creates the server with
`allowRetry: false`. `parseInt("0", 10)` is `0`, which is falsy, so PORT=0 binds 3000 and gives up if it
is taken. Observed on the packaged sidecar with the shell's own environment:
`Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:3000`, exit 1.

THE DESIGN IS SETTLED AND PROVEN BY A WORKING PROTOTYPE. See the `research.api_limitation` event for the
full transcript. In short:
  - `next()` + `getRequestHandler()` are public and sufficient for the handler.
  - WE create the listener: `http.createServer(...)` then `listen(0, "127.0.0.1")`, and read
    `server.address().port`. The kernel chooses; nothing probes.
  - LISTEN FIRST, PREPARE SECOND, with the handler awaiting the `prepare()` promise. This is what makes
    PW-0105 need NO changes -- its instrumentation still runs after the bind, so its handle-table
    discovery and its handshake work unaltered -- and it also closes PW-0105 requirement A's residual
    window, because no request is served before the bind-safety check has run.
  - The ONE non-public coupling is `__NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG`, set from
    `<distDir>/required-server-files.json`. `next({ conf })` is TYPED but silently ignored on the custom
    server path (`NextCustomServer.prepare` does not forward `conf` to `getRequestHandlers`), and the
    fully-public alternative -- a `next.config.js` in the packaged directory -- re-runs `assignDefaults`
    over an already-resolved config and measurably DROPS keys (`htmlLimitedBots`,
    `experimental.trustHostHeader`, and others). The implementation must assert at startup that the
    private variable took effect, so a future Next that removes it fails loudly.
  - Prototype result with 3000 occupied: two launches, ports 41623 and 40299, handshake correct both
    times, five routes 200, token/Host attacks 403.

WHY IT IS NOT STARTED: A SURFACE COLLISION WITH PW-0501, WHICH IS IN REVIEW.
The work needs `apps/desktop/sidecar-bootstrap/**` (new), `apps/desktop/scripts/package-sidecar.mjs`
(to lay the bootstrap and a layout file into the packaged tree) and
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs` (so the shell spawns the bootstrap rather than Next's entry).
All three are inside PW-0501's `allowedPaths` (`apps/desktop/**`).

This is not a housekeeping objection. `reviewProblems` in `scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs` recomputes
PW-0501's fingerprint at HEAD and refuses DONE with "stale review: implementation under <surface> changed
after approval" whenever it differs from what was approved. So committing PW-0106 into `apps/desktop/**`
WOULD BLOCK PW-0501 FROM EVER REACHING DONE on gpt-architect's current approval -- whether that approval
lands before or after the commit. The control plane is right and the sequencing is real.

`dependencies: ["PW-0501"]` therefore holds this task until PW-0501 is DONE, which needs one thing:
gpt-architect's `architecture-review` on PW-0501 at 65a47d5. gpt's round-96 message says PW-0501 "may
proceed through REVIEW based on its Windows build/install evidence", which is a statement about its
lifecycle and NOT a gate result -- it names no commit and does not say APPROVED, so it was not recorded
as one.

IF gpt-architect would rather PW-0106 start first, the reversible alternative is to narrow PW-0501's
`allowedPaths` away from the three files above BEFORE approving it, so the two surfaces stop overlapping.
That is their call, not mine: it changes what an approval fingerprints.

typecheck.evidence:
`npm run typecheck` -> "Tasks: 22 successful, 22 total". `npm run lint` -> "Tasks: 12 successful, 12 total", 0 errors (the one pre-existing warning, an unused type import in apps/web's in-memory-repository.test.ts, is outside this surface and predates the task). `npm run repo:validate` -> "Project Liberty repository validation passed." `npm run ai:validate` -> valid.

WHAT typecheck DOES AND DOES NOT COVER HERE, because this task's deliverable is not TypeScript. PW-0106 changed three files: a checked-in JavaScript entry point, a Node packaging script, and Rust. None is in a tsc project, so the 22 green turbo tasks establish only that nothing in apps/web or the packages regressed -- which is the correct thing for them to establish, since this task deliberately changed none of them. The static checking that applies to what DID change:

  - `node --check` on apps/desktop/sidecar-bootstrap/liberty-sidecar.js and acceptance.mjs: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the host target: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. This is the target that matters and it is checkable here even though the binary cannot be run here.
  - `package-sidecar.mjs` loads and reaches its first guard (it refuses without LIBERTY_SIDECAR_NODE, which is the designed behaviour).

THE CROSS-LANGUAGE CONSTANTS ARE CHECKED BY EXECUTION RATHER THAN BY A COMPILER, which is the only way they can be: `package-sidecar.mjs` asserts SERVER_RELATIVE_PATH and NODE_RELATIVE_PATH against `src/sidecar.rs` by regex, and a real packaging run passed with the new value `sidecar/server/liberty-sidecar.js`.

unit.evidence:
THREE SUITES, AND ONE OF THEM IS THE ONE THAT COULD ACTUALLY HAVE FOUND THIS DEFECT.

1. `cargo test` in apps/desktop/src-tauri -> 53 passed, 0 failed (was 51). Two new tests, both
   regression guards on the shell side:
     - `the_shell_spawns_our_bootstrap_and_never_nexts_generated_entry`: SERVER_RELATIVE_PATH must end
       in `/liberty-sidecar.js` and must NOT end in `/server.js`, and the planned launch must spawn the
       bootstrap. Pointing this constant back at Next's entry restores the defect silently -- packaging
       would still succeed, the installer would still install, and only a user would find out.
     - `the_shell_states_a_kernel_chosen_port_and_never_a_number_it_picked`: BIND_PORT is "0", the
       planned environment carries PORT=0, and no port appears in argv. This is acceptance item 12
       asserted rather than asserted-about: there is no socket, no bind and no retry anywhere in the
       shell, so there is nothing to probe with.
   One EXISTING test had to change and the change is worth naming: `a_missing_runtime_names_what_is_
   missing_and_where` matched the literal "server.js" to simulate an absent server. After the entry
   was renamed that predicate matched nothing, so the test got a valid launch and would have claimed a
   missing-server error it never saw -- a test that renames itself out of its own assertion. It now
   derives the filename from SERVER_RELATIVE_PATH.

2. `npm run test` -> 22/22 turbo tasks; @liberty/web 74 files / 1308 tests, @liberty/backend 3 files /
   36 tests, all passing. Unchanged by this task by design: PW-0106 touched no TypeScript, and
   gpt-architect's ruling requires PW-0105's controls be preserved rather than modified.

3. `node apps/desktop/sidecar-bootstrap/acceptance.mjs` -> 13/13, against the REAL packaged sidecar.
   This is where the actual acceptance lives and it is a script rather than a unit test for a reason
   stated in its header: the defect is in Next's generated entry, is invisible to every test in this
   repository, and was found by starting the artifact. A test that could not have found it is not the
   test this task needs. Results:
     1  port 3000 occupied for the test                held by the harness itself
     2  the packaged sidecar starts with 3000 occupied a handshake was emitted
     3  the actual listener port is not 3000           bound 40197
     4  the handshake carries the REAL bound port      GET /api/health on 40197 -> 200
     5  the handshake satisfies the parser grammar     {"host":"127.0.0.1","port":40197}
     6  all required routes serve                      / /search /profiles /api/health /signin all 200
     7  static / CSS / client assets load              stylesheet 200 (8085 B), chunk 200 (9871 B)
     8  token and Host attack cases still fail         8 cases, all 403: no token, wrong token,
                                                       evil.test, 127.0.0.1.evil.test, userinfo,
                                                       localhost, 0.0.0.0, wrong port in Host
     9  a non-loopback startup fails                   HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0, LIBERTY_SIDECAR_HOST=0.0.0.0
                                                       and HOSTNAME unset: exit 1, no handshake, each
    10  nothing writes beside the executable           1549 files unchanged under sidecar/ after traffic
    11  repeated launches use different ports          first 40197, second 36937
    12  no shell-side free-port probing exists         BIND_PORT is "0"; sidecar.rs names no TcpListener,
                                                       bind, SocketAddr, portpicker or port_check
     R  PORT=0 cannot silently become 3000 again       the shipped entry binds a literal 0 through
                                                       KERNEL_CHOOSES_THE_PORT and never reads
                                                       process.env.PORT

4. PACKAGING-TIME ASSERTIONS, which run on every `package-sidecar.mjs` invocation including the Windows
   job: the bootstrap source must declare `KERNEL_CHOOSES_THE_PORT = 0`, must call
   `server.listen(KERNEL_CHOOSES_THE_PORT, BIND_HOST, ...)`, and must not contain `process.env.PORT`;
   and the SHIPPED copy of `next/dist/server/config.js` must still name
   `__NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG`, so a Next upgrade that removes the one private coupling fails
   the build instead of producing an installer that comes up on default configuration.

WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated because it is the same gap PW-0501 has. Every measurement above is Linux.
Nothing here started liberty-desktop.exe, and the shell-to-sidecar handshake has still never been
exchanged on Windows. `apps/desktop` is not an npm workspace, so no vitest project reaches
`sidecar-bootstrap/`; the guards that run unattended today are the Rust tests and the packaging
assertions, and wiring `acceptance.mjs` into the Windows job is a follow-up outside this task's
allowedPaths (`.github/workflows/windows.yml` belongs to PW-0501).
